scope: HBQ final-route memory branch and CBE convoy endpoint retry command boundary
findings: HBQ remembers the final MOVE and restores it when the route ends while stopped far away. It may recreate a deleted waypoint with stored statements and properties, refresh the route, then escalate failed progress into route-lost relocation.
CBE only retries a still-existing unchanged plain MOVE. It does not recreate deleted waypoints, replay scripts or authorize relocation.
CBE checked waypoint identity before scheduled command issue. A replacement controller, registry, seat or native command could intervene before setCurrentWaypoint and doMove.
implementation: Final endpoint retry now rechecks captured brain, configuration, token, registry revision/membership, group/vehicle/crew locality, current seats, TRAVEL phase, feature gate, completed route, exact authored receipt, intentional waits, unchanged native command/destination receipts and absence of competing corridor/bypass work in one unscheduled transaction.
Retry count and cadence update only after command admission. No new world query, native movement writer, teleport or waypoint recreation.

Public CBE_Convoy_EndpointRecovery stores revision, exact route receipt, original start/deadline, attempts, next eligible server time and terminal exhaustion. Only changed revision/route may create a new allowance; expiry/count refusal issues no movement and does not renew clocks.
remaining: Initial finite endpoint retry policy implemented: six admitted recalls within the original120 seconds with15-second public cooldown, retained across owner/local-state replacement. Physical timing and migration acceptance remain outstanding.
An unchanged native receipt is admission evidence, not proof of physical travel or native reverse capability.
Physical route completion, deletion/edit, seat/owner migration, Zeus interruption and performance remain untested; audits paused.
